title: MEMORY.md update: R31 SAE-FiRE finding + Drift Regimes factor concept (R33 candidate)
rationale: Two durable findings from tonight's scan: (1) SAE-FiRE provides a concrete better-than-FinBERT approach for R31 text PEAD classification that should replace naive FinBERT chunking in the implementation plan. (2) The Drift Regimes factor (arXiv:2511.12490) represents a high-Sharpe standalone strategy suitable as a new research round (R33 or R34) after R32 options. These are 30-day-relevant facts that affect the research agenda.
content:
## Dream Cycle Research Scan — 2026-04-12

### R31 Implementation Update: SAE-FiRE supersedes naive FinBERT chunking
- SAE-FiRE (arXiv:2505.14420): Sparse Autoencoder feature extraction from Gemma 2-9B activations + XGBoost feature selection (top-4500 features) achieves F1 0.757 on earnings transcripts, beating Hierarchical FinBERT (F1 0.721). Use this approach in R31 instead of raw FinBERT scoring.
- Financial news AUC (0.703) > transcripts AUC (0.668) in their study. Combine transcript + news features for R31.
- Dataset: 9,324 earnings transcripts 2012-2014; validated on 10-Q MD&A and FNSPID news.

### New Research Round Candidate: Drift Regimes Factor (arXiv:2511.12490)
- Regime-conditioned value+reversal factor on S&P500: trade ONLY when UpFraction_i > 0.60 (>60% positive-return days in trailing 63d).
- EDGE = (0.7*value_pctile + 0.3*(-10d_return z-score)) * I(UpFraction > 0.60)
- OOS Sharpe 13.19 at 0.6bp costs; Sharpe 6.3 at 10bp. R2 to standard factors < 3%.
- Candidate for R33 or R34 after options round completes.
- Also useful as PEAD signal filter: require stock to be in drift regime 63 days pre-earnings.
